intent: Put billsplit on the one shared palette every other kuhy Flutter app now uses, instead of a teal-seeded scheme plus fifteen ad hoc colour literals.
scope: Non-goal: no behaviour, layout or business-logic change; no switch to a dark theme
changes: theme: ColorScheme.fromSeed(seedColor: Colors.teal) -> buildLightTheme() from design_system-v0.1.0. Light, not dark: the receipt screens carry black-on-white helper text that would be unreadable inverted.

Mapped the error-family literals onto ColorScheme slots: Colors.red -> error (4 sites), Colors.red.shade50 -> errorContainer with onErrorContainer text, and the swipe-to-delete Colors.red.shade300 + Colors.white -> error + onError, so the fill and the icon on top of it cannot drift apart.
Mapped the de-emphasised helper text Colors.black54 -> onSurfaceVariant (3 sites). These were the literals that would have broken outright on any dark surface.

Left the four-colour category ramp (deepOrange/amber/blueGrey/teal for alcohol/mixer/deposit/other) as literals, with a comment saying why: they encode category identity, not a theme role, and a single-accent design system has no four distinct hues to lend. Folding them into ColorScheme slots would destroy the only job they do. Tracked in unified-design-system/nielsen-audit.md as needing a categorical ramp.

verification.evidence: 4 issues, all pre-existing unnecessary_unawaited infos from SDK drift (the same class of info also present in epopeja_karta and kuhylog before this work). One real error introduced mid-edit -- const_eval_method_invocation, from putting Theme.of(context) inside a const Padding -- was found by the analyzer and fixed before commit.

verification.command: flutter test (ad-hoc palette assertion, then deleted)
verification.evidence: Pumped the real BillSplitApp and read the theme off a Scaffold element: primary=ffb8862e, surface=fff6f4f3 (paper), brightness=light. Confirms the palette actually changed rather than merely compiling.
15 -> 4, and the 4 remaining are exactly the category-dot ramp that was deliberately not mapped

risks: The app moves from a teal-derived Material scheme to the hand-picked gold palette, so every screen changes colour. That is the intent, and it is the last of four apps being brought onto one palette.

Colors.teal was both the theme seed and the default category dot. The seed is gone but the dot is deliberately unchanged, so those two are now decoupled -- previously they matched by coincidence, not by design. Noted here so the next reader does not read it as an oversight.

billsplit declares sdk ^3.5.0 while design_system declares ^3.12.2. Resolution succeeds on the installed SDK, but a machine on an older Dart could fail pub get; bumping billsplit's floor is the fix if that ever bites.
rollback: git revert the commit and run flutter pub get; there is no build artifact or device state to unwind, since billsplit ships no APK from this change.
After rollback, confirm flutter test still reports 60/60 and the coverage gate still reports 100% across 11 files.
